title: Taxation in India: From Budget to GST

questions.question: Which of the following is a DIRECT tax?
questions.rationale: Direct taxes fall on income/wealth and cannot be shifted (income, corporate, capital gains); GST, customs, and excise are indirect, collected at transactions and passed on through prices.

questions.question: A tax that takes a larger percentage of income from the rich than the poor is:
questions.rationale: Progressivity is the design of income tax slabs; indirect taxes like GST tend to be regressive since everyone pays the same rate regardless of income.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution mandates that no tax can be levied except by authority of law?
questions.rationale: Article 265 is the first word of Indian tax law: 'No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.'

questions.question: The GST Council, created by Article 279A, has voting weights of:
questions.rationale: The Centre holds 1/3 of the vote and states together 2/3, with decisions carried by a 3/4 majority — cooperative federalism by design.

questions.question: Input tax credit under GST means:
options: A firm deducts tax already paid on inputs from the tax it collects, so only value added is taxed
questions.rationale: Credit for tax on inputs eliminates the pre-GST cascade — each stage pays tax only on the value it adds, which is the essence of a value-added tax.

questions.question: On an inter-state sale, the component collected is:
questions.rationale: Inter-state supplies attract IGST, which the Centre collects and then devolves appropriately to the destination state.

questions.question: India's maximum marginal personal income tax rate in 1973–74 was about:
questions.rationale: The 1973–74 peak of 97.75% (including surcharge) is legendary; reforms since 1991 have progressively cut rates to today's 30% top slab.

questions.question: Which item is NOT currently within GST?
questions.rationale: Petroleum products, electricity, real estate (mostly), and alcohol for human consumption stay outside GST — a major critique of the credit chain's completeness.

questions.question: The Finance Commission (Article 280) is concerned with:
options: Dividing the divisible pool of central taxes between the Union and the states
questions.rationale: Every five years the Finance Commission recommends the vertical (Centre-state) and horizontal (inter-state) sharing of tax devolution and grants.

questions.question: GST is often criticised as regressive because:
options: It is too easy to evade
Uniform rates take a larger share of a poor household's budget than a rich one's
questions.rationale: Consumption taxes fall equally on the last rupee spent; since the poor consume most of their income, GST bites harder proportionally — softened by exemptions on food, health, and education.
